newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures tumble in active trading.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures tumble in active trading.

text.p: UK grain futures tumbled in active trading in a downward correction on Thursday which traders said was long overdue.
By the close wheat was over one stg down on a heavy volume.
"People have been saying for sometime the market was overdone but its taken until now for anything to happen," said a trader.
Others said the realisation that UK grain was too expensive had finally hit the market.
"French grain is down because they have a record crop but until now we have not really followed it," said another trader.
This year the French soft wheat crop has been estimated at 34 million tonnes, against a 1995 crop of 29.8 million.
Traders said another factor was the lack of export business and early results which show a good yield for the UK crop, but some quality drop.
However with 60 percent of the wheat still to be gathered in the north of England and Scotland it is too early for any accurate predicition on yeild and quality.
"People have been saying for sometime that there is going to be a lot of feed wheat around this year which is adding to pressure on prices," said one trader.
Wheat futures closed with losses of between 0.90 and 1.15 stg a tonne on a volume of 1,492 lots.
Barley futures traded 122 lots before closing 0.55 to one stg lower.
In Amsterdam the milling wheat futures contract was tradeless for the fourth day running.

Cash trading in the UK was also active with Sep feed wheat fetching 107.25 stg a tonne fob east coast ports, while 110.50 and 110.25 stg was paid for Oct/Dec, 113, 112.75 and 112.50 stg for Jan/Mar and 115.50 and 115 stg for Apr/Jun in all coasters up to 2,400 tonnes.
On paper delivered trade looked thin but traders said there was a good volume behind the figures.
Milling wheat 11 pct protein was fetching around 129 stg a tonne in the south of England for Sep while 132 stg was paid in Liverpool.
Feed wheat traded from 109 down to 108 stg for Sep in the Avon range with 111 and 110.50 stg paid for Oct/Dec.
In Liverpool 108 stg was paid for Sept and between 114 and 113.50 stg for Oct/Dec.
Feed barley fetched 106.50 for Oct/Dec in East Anglia and Avon with 109.50 and 112.50 stg paid respectively for Jan/Mch.
